A baby tiger’s roar is more of a high-pitched squeak or mewl than the deep, commanding roar of an adult. These vocalisations help tiger cubs communicate with their mother and siblings, often signaling hunger, playfulness, or seeking attention. While not as powerful as an adult’s roar, these sounds are an adorable glimpse into the cub’s journey of learning and growing into a formidable predator. Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.

In one particularly amusing moment, a tiger clamped its jaws around a water fountain and stood perfectly still for almost a minute.
